lines: In West Virginia, in eighteen ninety-seven, a ghost helped solve a crime.
A young bride was found dead, and the doctor called it natural.
Her mother did not believe it.
Four nights in a row, a pale figure stood by her bed.
Legend says it was her daughter, with a different story.
She named her husband, and turned her head right around to prove it.
The body was examined again, and the findings backed her up.
The husband went on trial, and was found guilty.
Could a ghost really help win a case?
title: The Ghost Who Testified at a Murder Trial #shorts
description:
In 1897 in West Virginia, a mother said her dead daughter's ghost named the culprit, and a famous trial followed. Legend or truth?
